target.title: fix(compaction): count CJK text in token estimates
target.body:
Closes #103930

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CJK-heavy sessions retain far more recent conversation than `keepRecentTokens` intends after compaction. The cut-point estimator treated CJK text as four characters per token, so Chinese, Japanese, and Korean content could be retained at roughly three to four times the configured token budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now uses the repository's existing CJK-aware character accounting for every textual message shape. That helper now lives in `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which both the root runtime and standalone `agent-core` can import without duplicating Unicode-range behavior; the existing root module remains a compatibility re-export.

## User Impact

CJK-heavy conversations now compact to approximately the same retained-token budget as equivalent ASCII conversations. ASCII estimates and image accounting are unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: the unmodified production estimator returned 40 estimated tokens for 160 CJK characters—the same result as 160 ASCII characters—and selected cut point index 1 for four such messages with a 100-token budget.

After, driving the real exported production functions on this branch:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module …
{"cjkTokens":160,"extensionBTokens":160,"cutPoint":3}
```

Focused validation passed:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-image-tokens.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-trailing-toolresult.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-cjk-tokens.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  17 passed (17)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/utils/cjk-chars.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  18 passed (18)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  90 passed (90)

$ pnpm --filter @openclaw/normalization-core build
Build complete

$ pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:test:packages
```

This is deterministic token-estimation and cut-point logic, so the direct production-function proof covers the affected behavior without requiring a live provider session. A live multi-turn CJK provider conversation was not run. AI-assisted; I reviewed the implementation and validation output.
